Function Description achieved Gemma 4's highest partial-pass rate, while Reconstruction Steps achieved GPT-5.4's highest full-pass rate. For structural similarity to human-written code, Reconstruction Steps was most frequently associated with libraries closest to the originals in Lines of File and total Cyclomatic Complexity, while Testing and Reconstruction Steps were jointly most frequent for File Count and Function Count.

contribution.en: This paper empirically studies how different categories of agent instructions affect LLM-based code generation for Python libraries.
contribution.zh: 该文实证研究了不同类别的智能体指令如何影响基于LLM的Python库代码生成。

why_care.en: It may inform LLM agent workflows for compiler tasks or program synthesis, but is only weakly related to the main lines of compiler optimization and architecture.
why_care.zh: 它可能为面向编译器任务或程序合成的LLM智能体工作流提供参考，但与编译器优化和体系结构的主线关联较弱。

candidates.title: The Role of Agentic Instruction Categories for Code Generation: A Study of Five Python Libraries

recommendations.abstract: Compiler transformations interact, making GPU kernel optimization a search for combinations that preserve the computation while improving performance. We introduce HOW TO TRAIN YOUR LITTLE DRAGON, a training method that teaches a small language model both to construct complete optimization scripts and to improve existing ones. Instead of ranking candidates or generating kernel code, our model generates optimization scripts. We devise a compact, lossless representation whose deterministic decoding reconstructs the exact compiler trace, preserving its transformation parameters and dependencies. We use a compiler framework TVM MetaSchedule to build training data on 54,116 distinct workloads, and construct 108,594 examples in two training sets: 60,236 teach the model to generate an optimized script from an unoptimized kernel, while 48,358 teach it to produce a better script given the kernel and a somewhat optimized script. Supervised fine-tuning teaches the model to construct and improve optimization scripts from these search-derived examples. We then add reinforcement learning with a shaped reward that combines correctness with measured performance, awarding a latency-based bonus only to numerically correct kernels. We apply this training method to a model with 8 billion parameters. After supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, the model achieves per-attempt correctness of 91.27% for construction and 92.01% for refinement, while reinforcement learning produces faster kernels than supervised training on 88 of 102 construction tasks and 145 of 170 refinement prompts. With only 8B parameters, our LITTLE DRAGON achieves higher per-attempt correctness and better kernel performance than six frontier LLMs: GPT-6 Astra, Opus 5, Kimi-K3, and GLM-5.3 among them, each with hundreds of billions to trillions of parameters, for which task-specific training is unavailable or expensive.

contribution.en: Trains a small language model to construct and refine TVM MetaSchedule optimization scripts while preserving a losslessly decodable compiler trace.
contribution.zh: 训练小语言模型生成并改进 TVM MetaSchedule 优化脚本，并保持编译器 trace 可无损重建。

why_care.en: It directly targets transformation-combination search and GPU kernel optimization, aligning with autoscheduling and code generation interests.
why_care.zh: 它直接面向编译器变换组合搜索与 GPU 内核优化，与自动调度和代码生成兴趣高度相关。

recommendations.title: How to Train Your Little Dragon: Teaching a Small Language Model to Construct and Refine GPU Optimization Scripts

recommendations.abstract: Aggressive quantization of neural networks can expose activation functions as bottlenecks for efficient hardware acceleration. Implementing quantized activations as multi-threshold operations has been shown to be a promising optimization, allowing for efficient hardware implementation of few-bit activations. However, current implementations are limited to monotonically increasing functions, quantization schemes with one-dimensional (per-channel) granularity and a small set of predefined activation-quantizer combinations. We formalize the multi-threshold representation to extend it to non-monotonic functions and fine-granular parameters, i.e., multi-dimensional thresholds. For automated conversion of quantized function compositions into threshold representation, we propose a systematic approach via algebraic rules integrated into the ONNX-based compiler infrastructure. We experimentally validate our solution on a selection of monotonic and non-monotonic functions by extending the binary search based multi-threshold operator that is integrated into the FINN framework for end-to-end synthesis of custom-tailored FPGA accelerators. The cost of hardware support for non-monotonicity and fine-granularity is characterized in comparison to an alternative approach utilizing existing operators via graph-level decomposition. We compare our method to prior work as well as the approach taken by the hls4ml framework. As an outlook, we demonstrate the prospects of using the multi-threshold representation during the training of a neural network as a form of quantization aware training.

contribution.en: It extends multi-threshold representation to non-monotonic quantized activations in an ONNX-based accelerator compiler flow.
contribution.zh: 将多阈值表示扩展到非单调量化激活并集成到ONNX加速器编译流程。

why_care.en: Compiler-architecture co-design for custom DNN accelerators matches active code-generation interests.
why_care.zh: 面向定制DNN加速器的编译与架构协同设计，契合代码生成研究兴趣。

recommendations.title: Compiling Multi-Threshold Operators for Quantized Non-Monotonic and Fine-Granular Activations in Custom-Tailored DNN Accelerators

recommendations.abstract: Meta deploys a heterogeneous fleet comprising NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and proprietary MTIA accelerators to reduce costs and mitigate vendor lock-in. However, the extensive history of NVIDIA-specific optimizations hinders performance portability to other hardware. This paper presents our methods for optimizing alternative accelerators, using AMD Instinct MI350X versus NVIDIA B200 for recommendation model training as a case study. We propose three reusable principles. First, hardware-model co-design is essential: rather than directly porting models from NVIDIA GPUs, revising model structures and software recipes allows full exploitation of accelerator-specific strengths (e.g., MI350X's 1.6x HBM capacity relative to B200). Second, our analytical performance model enables zero-warmup optimal kernel selection across diverse datatypes and matrix shapes in production models, drastically simplifying tuning. Third, increasingly mature agentic workflows have lowered the barrier to porting from the CUDA ecosystem; we extend these workflows for microarchitecture-aware kernel optimizations and custom shim generation. Compared to the directly ported baseline, these methods deliver up to 1.5x improvement in end-to-end training throughput. To our knowledge, this is the first hyperscaler report on productionizing AMD GPUs for large-scale training. Our contributions have been upstreamed to the open-source PyTorch, Triton, and ROCm ecosystems.

contribution.en: Reports Meta's production AI-training optimization on AMD GPUs via hardware-model co-design, analytical kernel selection, and agentic porting workflows.
contribution.zh: 报告 Meta 在 AMD GPU 上通过硬件—模型协同设计、分析性能模型与 agentic 移植流程实现生产级 AI 训练优化。

why_care.en: It directly concerns heterogeneous performance portability, kernel selection, and compiler-ecosystem porting, adjacent to compiler-architecture co-design interests.
why_care.zh: 它直接涉及异构硬件性能可移植性、内核选择和编译生态移植，与体系结构协同设计兴趣相邻。

recommendations.title: Architecting for Hardware Diversity: Meta's End-to-End Co-Design for High-Performance AI Training on AMD GPUs

recommendations.abstract: We present Cyclotron, a compiler that expresses streaming dataflow algorithms using recurrence equations, which are then compiled to distributed topologies of interlinked processors. Our compiler lowers a language of recurrences over logical iteration spaces into per-processor programs of sends, receives, and computations. In these recurrences, data accesses are not limited to external accesses to memory; data can live separately on the iteration space itself, allowing internal points to communicate values directly with other points. Users specify this communication directly in the recurrence language, which allows them to express various communication patterns such as a nearest-neighbor systolic exchange, a one-to-all broadcast, a bidirectional split ring, or an asymmetric and piecewise broadcast pattern, which are often not supported by standard distributed linear algebra libraries. These recurrences describe the algorithm and communication independently of how they map onto the hardware. A programmer then chooses which dimensions execute across processors and which execute over time, without rewriting the entire program. Users only specify data dependencies across the iteration space, and the compiler safely generates a program, per process, with correct placement of both communication and computational operators according to the chosen space--time mapping. We evaluate distributed matrix multiplication, TRSM, Cholesky, and fused Cholesky--TRSM on up to 16 CPU nodes and 16 GPUs, comparing against ScaLAPACK, SLATE, and cuSolverMp. Cyclotron is competitive with and often outperforms these hand-optimized libraries; for Cholesky, the best communication strategy changes with problem size and architecture.

contribution.en: Presents Cyclotron, a recurrence language and compiler that lowers logical iteration spaces into distributed per-processor send/receive programs.
contribution.zh: 提出用递归方程表达处理器间通信的 Cyclotron 语言与编译器，将逻辑迭代空间映射为分布式 send/receive 程序。

why_care.en: Its space-time mapping and communication code generation are relevant to parallel compilation and retargetable code generation.
why_care.zh: 其空间—时间映射和通信代码生成对并行编译与可重定向代码生成有借鉴意义。

recommendations.title: Cyclotron: A Recurrence Language for Expressing Interprocessor Communication

recommendations.abstract: RISC-V processors are now widely available for FPGAs, with most FPGA vendors replacing their proprietary soft-CPU architectures with this instruction-set architecture (ISA). Although contemporary FPGAs are increasingly resource- and feature-rich, a soft processor system---including memory---often occupies a disproportionately large footprint and delivers only modest performance relative to the potential of the target device. In this work we first design a lightweight but deeply pipelined RISC-V core that can run above 700 MHz in a mid-range device and that is capable of retiring one instruction per clock under ideal conditions. We then develop and demonstrate a new optimization method that compiles the final application binary and a specialized processor instance contemporaneously. The method expands each instruction into an application-specific encoding, removes unused datapath and decode logic during synthesis, and yields cores that remain assembler-compatible with the original program while no longer being binary-compatible with a general-purpose RISC-V. We implement example designs on RV32I (base integer), RV32M (integer multiply), and RV32F (single-precision floating-point) configurations. Our optimized RISC-V is as small as 170 ALMs and closes timing at 775 MHz in an Altera Agilex-5 device. Finally, we show that these processors can be packed into a deterministic area and stepped-and-repeated continuously without material impact on performance, enabling predictable multi-core density planning.

contribution.en: Co-compiles an application binary with a specialized RISC-V processor instance, generating application-specific instruction encodings and removing unused logic.
contribution.zh: 提出将应用程序二进制与专用 RISC-V 处理器实例同时编译优化，生成应用特定指令编码并削减未用逻辑。

why_care.en: Its joint specialization of ISA and hardware datapath relates to virtual ISA, retargetable compilation, and hardware-software co-design.
why_care.zh: 其同时特化 ISA 与硬件数据通路的思想与虚拟 ISA、可重定向编译和软硬件协同设计相关。

recommendations.title: Minimum RISC-V: Maximum FPGA Efficiency
